# Aim

This document calibrates and generates the superpopulation used by all
simulation scenarios of the main analysis (S0-S4), and the S4 trial pool. It
produces:

- `data/dgp_calibration.rda`: calibrated Weibull parameters (`cal`);
- `data/superpopulation_generated_weibull.rda`: the superpopulation;
- `data/trial_pool_s4_generated_weibull_s4.rda`: the S4 trial pool;
- `results/tables/`: Table 1 and Supplementary Tables A1-A2.

Inputs: `config/parameters.R` (design parameters and S4 selection model) and
`config/simulation_structure.xlsx` (covariate distributions and prognostic
coefficients). The DGP functions are in `functions/dgp_weibull.R` and `function/dgp_s4.R`.


# Why a Weibull model

The control arm must reproduce two clinical targets: a median OS of
7.5 months and a 12-month survival of 0.32. Under an exponential
proportional hazards model,
\[
S_i(t \mid X_i) = \exp\{-\lambda_0\, t\, \exp(\eta_i)\},
\]
the baseline has a single parameter: once the median is fixed, the whole
curve is fixed (for \(\eta_i = 0\), \(S(12) = \exp\{-12 \log 2 / 7.5\}\)), so
the two targets cannot be matched independently.

The Weibull proportional hazards model adds a shape parameter \(k\):
\[
S_i(t \mid X_i, Z_i) = \exp\{-\lambda_0\, t^{k} \exp(\eta_i)\},
\qquad
h_i(t \mid X_i, Z_i) = \lambda_0\, k\, t^{k-1} \exp(\eta_i),
\]
with \(\eta_i = X_i^\top\beta + Z_i\beta_Z\). It reduces to the exponential
model for \(k = 1\); the hazard increases over time for \(k > 1\) and
decreases for \(k < 1\).

**Calibration.** The marginal control survival is a mixture over the
covariate distribution,
\(S_0(t) = E_X[\exp\{-\lambda_0 t^k \exp(X^\top\beta)\}]\), approximated on a
large calibration population by
\(\widehat S_0(t) = N^{-1} \sum_i \exp\{-\lambda_0 t^k \exp(\eta_{i0})\}\).
\(\lambda_0\) and \(k\) minimise
\[
\big[\widehat S_0(t_{0.5,0}) - 0.5\big]^2 +
\big[\widehat S_0(\tau) - S_{0,\tau}^{target}\big]^2,
\]
and \(\beta_Z\) is then chosen so that \(\widehat S_1(t_{0.5,1}) = 0.5\), with
\(\widehat S_1(t) = N^{-1}\sum_i \exp\{-\lambda_0 t^k \exp(\eta_{i0} + \beta_Z)\}\).
\(\beta_Z\) is a conditional log-hazard ratio: because of non-collapsibility
it differs from the marginal one.

**Event times** are generated by inverse transform sampling:
\[
T_i = \left[\frac{-\log U_i}{\lambda_0 \exp(\eta_i)}\right]^{1/k},
\qquad U_i \sim \mathrm{Uniform}(0, 1),
\]
with independent uniforms under control and treatment, and a common
administrative censoring time \(C_i \sim \mathrm{Uniform}(C_{low}, C_{upp})\).


# Setup

```{r libraries}
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(survival)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

source(here("config/parameters.R"))
source(here("functions/dgp_weibull.R"))
source(here("functions/dgp_s4.R"))
source(here("functions/table_dgp.R"))

dir.create(here("data"), showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(here("results/tables"), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

Covariate distributions and prognostic coefficients are read from the S1
sheet (registry row), common to all scenarios. Censoring bounds are read from
the trial row and applied to the whole superpopulation, registry included.
The S4 sheet only provides the target prevalences of Supplementary Table A2.

```{r parameters}
read_row <- function(sheet, row) {
  readxl::read_excel(here(PATH_DGP_XLSX), sheet = sheet) |>
    dplyr::filter(parameters == row)
}

reg_params   <- read_row("S1", "registry") |> check_dgp_params()
trial_params <- read_row("S1", "trial")
s4_reg       <- read_row("S4", "registry") |> check_dgp_params()
s4_trial     <- read_row("S4", "trial")    |> check_dgp_params()

dgp_args <- make_dgp_args(reg_params)
```


# Calibration

```{r calibration}
set.seed(SEED_MASTER)

cal <- do.call(
  calibrate_weibull_DGP,
  c(
    list(
      N_calib          = N_CALIB_MAIN,
      target_median_z0 = TARGET_MEDIAN_Z0,
      target_S0_tau    = TARGET_S0_TAU,
      target_median_z1 = TARGET_MEDIAN_Z1,
      tau              = TAU
    ),
    dgp_args
  )
)


cal$checks |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "check", values_to = "value") |>
  kable(digits = 4)

save(cal, file = here("data/dgp_calibration.rda"))
```

The calibrated shape is \(k =\) `r round(cal$weibull_shape, 3)`: the
individual hazard increases over time. This is a consequence of the
calibration constraints, not an assumption on recurrent glioblastoma:
high-risk patients leave the risk set early, which flattens the marginal
hazard, and the individual hazard must increase to reproduce the marginal
targets.


# Superpopulation

The superpopulation is generated in the same random stream as the
calibration (no seed reset in between).

```{r superpopulation}
superpopulation_generated <- do.call(
  generate_superpopulation,
  c(
    list(
      N                 = N_SUPERPOP_MAIN,
      C_low             = C_low,
      C_upp             = C_upp,
      lambda0           = cal$lambda0,
      weibull_shape     = cal$weibull_shape,
      beta_treatment_OS = cal$beta_treatment_OS
    ),
    dgp_args
  )
)

save(superpopulation_generated,
     file = here("data/superpopulation_generated_weibull.rda"))
```


# S4 trial pool

The S4 trial pool is drawn from the superpopulation with weights
\(\exp(\eta_{sel})\), where \(\eta_{sel}\) is a linear selection score with
the log-odds in `S4_SELECTION_COEFS`. The coefficients follow the direction
of the target prevalences (S4 sheet) but are attenuated to keep a plausible
overlap (Supplementary Table A2). The pool is restricted to \(B = 1\) later,
when the scenario pools are built.

```{r s4-pool}
trial_pool_s4 <- make_s4_trial_pool(
  superpop     = superpopulation_generated,
  N_trial_pool = N_TRIAL_POOL_S4,
  coefs        = S4_SELECTION_COEFS,
  seed         = SEED_MASTER
)

save(trial_pool_s4, file = here("data/trial_pool_s4_generated_weibull_s4.rda"))
```


# Checks

Latent and observed survival in the superpopulation and in the S4 trial pool.
The latent quantities use the true event times, the observed ones the
Kaplan-Meier estimate under administrative censoring.

```{r checks}
km_summary <- function(dat, pop) {
  purrr::map_dfr(c(z0 = "0", z1 = "1"), function(z) {
    fit <- survfit(Surv(dat[[paste0("time_z", z)]], dat[[paste0("event_z", z)]]) ~ 1)
    T_lat <- dat[[paste0("T_true_z", z)]]
    tibble(
      population   = pop,
      arm          = ifelse(z == "0", "Control", "Treatment"),
      median_true  = median(T_lat),
      median_KM    = unname(summary(fit)$table["median"]),
      S_tau_true   = mean(T_lat > TAU),
      S_tau_KM     = summary(fit, times = TAU)$surv,
      prop_events  = mean(dat[[paste0("event_z", z)]])
    )
  })
}

bind_rows(
  km_summary(superpopulation_generated, "Superpopulation"),
  km_summary(trial_pool_s4,             "S4 trial pool")
) |>
  kable(digits = 3)
```

## Table 1. DGP parameters

```{r table-1}
tab_dgp_parameters <- table_dgp_parameters(reg_params, references)

tab_dgp_parameters |>
  kable(
    digits    = 3,
    col.names = c("Section", "Covariate", "Prevalence / mean", "SD",
                  "log-HR", "HR", "Note", "Reference"),
    caption   = paste0(
      "Table 1. Registry covariate distributions and prognostic coefficients ",
      "of the Weibull outcome model, common to all scenarios. Extent of ",
      "resection and treatment intensity are ordinal with a linear effect per ",
      "level (per-level log-HR: ", reg_params$beta_resection_OS, " and ",
      reg_params$beta_trt_baseline_OS, "); the log-HR shown for each level is ",
      "the contrast with the reference level. Localization indicators are ",
      "generated independently and have no prognostic effect. Administrative ",
      "censoring: Uniform(", trial_params$C_low, ", ", trial_params$C_upp_trial,
      ") months in both cohorts."
    )
  )
```

## Supplementary Table A1. Weibull calibration

```{r table-a1}
tab_weibull_calibration <- table_weibull_calibration(cal, superpopulation_generated, TAU)

tab_weibull_calibration |>
  kable(
    digits    = 4,
    col.names = c("Parameter", "Target", "Calibrated", "Verified on superpopulation"),
    caption   = paste0(
      "Supplementary Table A1. Calibrated Weibull parameters (calibration ",
      "population N = ", format(N_CALIB_MAIN, big.mark = ","), ", seed = ",
      SEED_MASTER, ") and checks on the latent event times of the ",
      "superpopulation (N = ", format(N_SUPERPOP_MAIN, big.mark = ","), ")."
    )
  )
```

## Supplementary Table A2. S4 covariate shift

```{r table-a2}
tab_s4_shift <- table_s4_shift(
  reg_target   = s4_reg,
  trial_target = s4_trial,
  superpop     = superpopulation_generated,
  trial_pool   = trial_pool_s4,
  coefs        = S4_SELECTION_COEFS,
  references   = references
)

tab_s4_shift |>
  kable(
    digits    = 3,
    col.names = c("Section", "Covariate", "Registry (target)", "Trial (target)",
                  "Registry (observed)", "Trial (observed)", "Selection log-OR",
                  "Note", "Reference"),
    caption   = paste0(
      "Supplementary Table A2. Scenario S4: target prevalences from the ",
      "literature and prevalences observed in the superpopulation (N = ",
      format(N_SUPERPOP_MAIN, big.mark = ","), ") and in the S4 trial pool ",
      "(N = ", format(N_TRIAL_POOL_S4, big.mark = ","), ", before restriction ",
      "to B = 1). Means are reported for continuous covariates. Selection ",
      "log-OR: coefficient of the S4 selection model."
    )
  )
```

```{r save-tables}
save(tab_dgp_parameters, tab_weibull_calibration, tab_s4_shift,
     file = here("results/tables/tables_dgp.rda"))

write.csv(tab_dgp_parameters,      here("results/tables/table1_dgp_parameters.csv"),      row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(tab_weibull_calibration, here("results/tables/tableA1_weibull_calibration.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(tab_s4_shift,            here("results/tables/tableA2_s4_shift.csv"),            row.names = FALSE)
```


# Figures

## Exponential versus Weibull

Illustrative curves with the same scale \(\lambda_0 = \log 2 / 7.5\) and
three shapes; \(k = 1\) is the exponential model.

```{r fig-exp-weibull, fig.height = 4, fig.width = 11}
lambda_exp <- log(2) / TARGET_MEDIAN_Z0
t_grid     <- seq(0.1, 36, by = 0.1)

curves <- tidyr::expand_grid(time = t_grid, k = c(0.7, 1, 1.4)) |>
  mutate(
    Survival = exp(-lambda_exp * time^k),
    Hazard   = lambda_exp * k * time^(k - 1),
    Density  = Hazard * Survival,
    shape    = factor(paste0("k = ", k))
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Survival, Hazard, Density), names_to = "quantity") |>
  mutate(quantity = factor(quantity, levels = c("Survival", "Hazard", "Density")))

ggplot(curves, aes(time, value, colour = shape)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~ quantity, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (months)", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Latent survival in the generated populations

```{r fig-latent-survival, fig.height = 4.5, fig.width = 10}
latent_curve <- function(dat, pop) {
  purrr::map_dfr(c(Control = "T_true_z0", Treatment = "T_true_z1"), function(v) {
    fit <- survfit(Surv(dat[[v]], rep(1, nrow(dat))) ~ 1)
    tibble(time = fit$time, surv = fit$surv)
  }, .id = "arm") |>
    mutate(population = pop)
}

bind_rows(
  latent_curve(superpopulation_generated, "Superpopulation"),
  latent_curve(trial_pool_s4,             "S4 trial pool")
) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, surv, colour = arm)) +
  geom_step(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(TARGET_MEDIAN_Z0, TARGET_MEDIAN_Z1), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = TAU, linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~ population) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 36)) +
  labs(x = "Time (months)", y = "Survival probability", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
